label: Small business smash and grab spree, Eastside and Snohomish County, 2018
area: Kirkland, Sammamish, Redmond, Bothell, Issaquah, Lynnwood, Mill Creek, Everett, Monroe, WA

linking_evidence: a fingerprint on an office drawer in Kirkland matched one defendant
DNA from blood on a table leg at a Kirkland restaurant matched the same defendant
a fingerprint lifted from a cash register in Monroe matched the same defendant
the same car appeared on security footage at two scenes within an hour, and cell tower records allegedly placed the car owner's phone moving between the scenes
the defendant was caught in a stolen van with a window punching tool and glass in his shoe moments after a break-in, and was arrested three blocks from another scene with glass in his cuffs
prosecutors called it a months-long smash-and-grab burglary spree that spans jurisdictions
ground_truth.notes: The listed incidents are those the Herald article describes with dates; the article does not say which of the two defendants committed each one. Direct evidence ties are stated only for esg-01, esg-02, esg-03, esg-07, esg-10 and esg-11. The other incidents are described as part of the spree without a stated physical tie. One defendant admitted to about 50 burglaries that are not itemized, and police said they were still working out how many crimes tie to the two men. Police around Snohomish County counted at least 21 other smash and grabs over a six-week summer span. This series falls outside the 2021 to 2026 range of the rest of the Seattle research and is included as a richer evidence example. Dates for esg-01 and esg-02 are months only.

outcome.summary: One defendant was arrested 5 Oct 2018 and charged that week with four burglary counts, one attempted burglary, trafficking in stolen property and methamphetamine possession, with bail of 225,000 dollars. The second defendant was arrested 8 Sep 2018 on 19 felony counts. Later outcome not found.

data_policy: Public sources only. No suspect or victim names, ages, or exact addresses.
